Control Parameters for Normal-Block Models

Source: R/normal_block.R
NB_control.Rd

Control the model settings and various optimization parameters

Usage

NB_control(
  niter = 500,
  threshold = 1e-04,
  fixed_point_niter = 5,
  sparsity_weights = NULL,
  sparsity_penalties = NULL,
  n_sparsity_penalties = 30,
  min_ratio = 0.01,
  fixed_tau = FALSE,
  clustering_init = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE,
  heuristic = FALSE,
  noise_covariance = NULL,
  refine = TRUE,
  acceleration = NULL
)

Arguments

niter

maximal number of (V)EM iterations.

threshold

the (V)EM stops when the objective (log-likelihood or ELBO) increases by less than this. A negative value runs exactly `niter` iterations, without the warning issued when `niter` is reached.

fixed_point_niter

number of sweeps of the tau update for Normal-Block-Mean models with unknown clusters. Each sweep visits the rows of tau sequentially and maximizes the ELBO exactly in each, so it can never decrease the ELBO.

sparsity_weights

a symmetric matrix of weights applied to the penalty, entry by entry: q x q (variance-block) or p x p (mean-block). By default, 1 off the diagonal and 0 on it (the diagonal is not penalized).

sparsity_penalties

the penalties of a sparsity path (`sparsity = TRUE`). By default, `n_sparsity_penalties` values from the smallest penalty that removes every edge down to `min_ratio` times it, on a log scale.

n_sparsity_penalties

number of penalties of the default path.

min_ratio

ratio between the smallest and the largest penalty of the default path.

fixed_tau

whether the posterior cluster probabilities stay at their initial value (`clustering_init`) during the optimization; used to refit a sparsity path with its clustering held fixed (stability selection).

clustering_init

how to obtain the initial clustering of the q unknown blocks: a heuristic name ("ward2", "kmeans", "sbm" or "spectral"), an actual clustering (a vector of labels or a p x q indicator matrix, or a list of either per q for a collection), or "best_of_inits" to try several heuristics per model and keep the best-ELBO fit (see [NormalBlockBase]'s `best_of_inits()`; not supported with `sparsity = TRUE`). Default `NULL`, i.e. "kmeans" for both model families; "ward2" can work better on zero-inflated abundance data.

verbose

whether to print the progress of the optimization.

heuristic

whether to use the heuristic approach (moment-based, no (V)EM recursion) instead of the full (V)EM. Default is FALSE. In heuristic mode, no likelihood/ELBO is computed, so `entropy`, `loglik`, `BIC`, `ICL` and `EBIC` are all `NA` on the resulting model.

noise_covariance

shape of the residual covariance. Variance-block models accept "diagonal" (variable-specific) or "spherical" (common); mean-block models, whose Sigma is the full p x p residual covariance, also accept "full". Default `NULL`, resolved per model family at fit time to "diagonal" – except for a mean-block model with `sparsity > 0`, which implies "full" since a penalty on a diagonal precision matrix would have nothing to act on (explicitly asking for both is an error). A full Sigma has many parameters and needs n > p; use it when the residual associations between variables are of interest.

refine

for collections over a range of cluster counts (both families): whether `optimize()` automatically calls `refine()` afterwards. Default `TRUE`: the split and merge search repairs the poor local optima that independent fits can leave, at a few times the cost of the collection. With `FALSE`, `collection$refine()` can be called later.

acceleration

whether the (V)EM is accelerated by SQUAREM (Varadhan & Roland, 2008), an extrapolation built on two successive (V)EM steps and accepted only if it does not lower the objective. Default `NULL`: on, except for mean-block models with a diagonal or spherical Sigma, whose EM is exact and fast. `TRUE` or `FALSE` forces it. Never used when `sparsity > 0`.

Value

A named list of parameters to pass to [normal_block()]'s `control` argument.

Examples

ex_data <- generate_normal_block_var_data(n = 50, p = 20, d = 1, q = 3)
data <- NormalBlockData$new(ex_data$Y, ex_data$X)
## silent fits, without the split and merge search
ctrl <- NB_control(verbose = FALSE, refine = FALSE)
collection <- normal_block(data, blocks = 2:4, control = ctrl)
collection$criteria
#>   nb_param q n_edges sparsity    loglik  deviance      BIC      ICL     EBIC
#> 1       44 2       1        0 -562.3405 1124.6810 1295.894 1295.894 1297.280
#> 2       48 3       3        0 -467.6143  935.2286 1121.173 1121.173 1127.765
#> 3       53 4       6        0 -467.6177  935.2355 1139.824 1139.824 1156.459
#>   niter
#> 1    11
#> 2     7
#> 3    34
